6% to 7% operating margin target a “milestone rather than a ceiling” and sees the company exceeding this in time, although that trajectory will unlikely be linear.
The analyst credits the markedly improved pace of same-store sales to renovations, traction in e-commerce, and the value proposition that puts Dollar General
does see this as necessary as prices are currently within 3 to 4 percentage points of mass market competitors, leaving the company with "dry powder" if needed.
The competitive prices at Dollar General
are not only bringing in new customers but  helping with customer retention as new shoppers become aware of the merchandise selection.
Moreover, Thomas sees the introduction of a loyalty program as another potential boost to customer retention and operating leverage, creating what he calls a “double benefit.”
Considering all these positive factors, Thomas believes shares do not reflect the turnaround. The shares currently trade at 15x P/E, which is at the low end of the historical range.

“If shares simply erased their underperformance vs. CPI and the group delivered its 7% margin target, then we could be looking at a stock trading on 11x. This looks too cheap, given the resilience of the business and future opportunities.
Besides an upgrade, Thomas also raises his target price for Dollar General
by 28% to $160, representing ~33% upside to Wednesday’s close.
Wall Street analysts and Seeking Alpha authors all view Dollar General
as a Buy, while Seeking Alpha’s Quant score of 4.37 out of 5 also represents a Buy rating.
